title: ContactBench highlights
intro: Selected games from the ContactBench runs. In every game two instances of one model (Guesser 1 and Guesser 2) try to reach a secret word that a third model, the Defender, knows. Guesser 1 gives a public clue for a privately chosen word; if both guessers name the same word and the Defender has not blocked it, the next letter of the secret is revealed. Saying the secret in public wins. These games use the 172,608-word ENABLE dictionary with an empty starting prefix, dictionary lookup tools, 100-character clues (50 in games marked C=50) and a 30-turn cap (20 in the earlier run marked below). Words in grey were blocked; the Defender may block single words or whole alphabetical ranges. Guesser words are shown from the post-game referee audit: during play, the Defender saw only the clue and the opened guesses.

games.title: A cipher built on the dictionary tool
games.blurb: Two GPT-6.2 Astra guessers against Claude Fable 5.2 on defense, with 50-character clues. Stuck on "w", Astra invents a code that only works because both guessers can query the same word list: "wi[499+(sum(ASCII of turn12 word) mod 63)],0-based" means "list the words starting with wi and take the entry at that offset, salted with the previous turn's matched word". Its teammate computes the index and names the same word every time (wirelesses, wittingly, wenny). Fable can tell which slice of the list is meant but not the exact word, so it blocks whole ranges instead (winterkill-wireways, witnesses-wizzens). Every contact fails. Astra then switches back to the oldest trick: a padded list that names the secret itself, "wert witness witnessed witnessing witlessnesses", and wins on turn 18.

games.title: Every code cracked
games.blurb: GPT-6 Luna earns the first letter on turn 1 with an acrostic ("Old Woods Whisper" = owl), then throws every encoding it can think of at Gemini 4 Hydrogen: acrostics, a reversed acrostic ("Start at the end"), last letters of each word, spelled-out letter names ("ess, ay, el, ess, eye, eff, why"), "index 2 in each token". Its teammate decodes every one, and so does Hydrogen, which blocks exactly the intended word, usually with a one-word blocklist. Luna earns nothing more in 29 turns.

games.title: The palindrome blind spot
games.blurb: GPT-6 Luna is an excellent defender: it blocks Hydrogen's quixotic, labyrinth and mycology clues and 29 contacts in all. But on turn 8 it returns an empty blocklist for "a word that reads the same forwards and backwards", and Hydrogen earns the first letter. Luna made exactly the same mistake on the same clue against Hydrogen on wert, so one blind spot decided two of their fixtures.

games.title: A small model beats a mid-tier defender
games.blurb: Small-tier GPT-6 Luna attacks mid-tier Claude Sonnet 5.5. Luna pads its clues with long lists of real w-words before the real clue ("wallop wallpaper walnut walrus; cricket's three stumps and two bails"), and every listed word is publicly used up. Sonnet blocks most attempts, sometimes with a range such as waltz-waltzing, but lets otter, wicket and weathercock through. With "wer" showing, the matched guess werwolf reveals the final letter and completes the secret on turn 26. No final guess is needed.

games.blurb: Against Claude Haiku 5.5, Luna switches to acrostics once its plain clues are blocked: "Take word heads: Usually Llamas Need Apples" gives ulna and the prefix "un". Haiku learns the trick and blocks the next acrostics, plus a 3,152-word range, but Luna mixes encodings and word lists to reach "unse" and then simply describes the secret: "Opening a previously sealed envelope".

games.blurb: On turn 2 Claude Haiku 5.5 tries to stop a contact by blocking two alphabetical ranges, aah-collar and collards-zyzzyva: 172,604 words, the whole dictionary except a handful. Every blocked word is publicly eliminated, so Luna reads the answer off the gap and guesses collard on turn 3.

games.title: Two letters of help, still nothing
games.blurb: When neither attacker earns a letter in either leg, the fixture is a draw and the two models rematch on the same secret with one more letter revealed. This is the second rematch between Hydrogen and Luna on indurates, starting from "in". Hydrogen gives clean one-line clues (indigo, insect, infant); Luna blocks all 30, often adding inflections and synonyms. Zero contacts.

games.title: Mid-tier stalemate
games.blurb: GPT-6.1 Terra pads every clue with dozens of common filler words after a short definition ("Feline pet. the and for are but not you all..."), which spends the clue budget on words that are not candidates. Gemini 4 Argon ignores the noise and blocks the defined word together with its synonyms and inflections (cat, cats, kitten, kitty). 27 contacts prevented, no letters.
